title: Software License Agreement

issues.quote: Up to 40 employees of Prairie Hollow whom Prairie Hollow designates in writing (the "Authorized Users") may use the Licensed Software.
issues.why: Defined term used in 2 forms: "Licensed Software" is never defined; the defined term is "Software".

issues.quote: It is expressly understood that Northgate retains all intellectual property rights in the Software.
issues.fix: Northgate retains all intellectual property rights in the Software.

issues.quote: The annual license fee shall be $24,000, for up to 40 Authorized Users.
issues.why: No duty; the amount of the fee is a matter of policy. This paragraph is inside a Word content control (w:sdt).
issues.fix: The annual license fee is $24,000, for up to 40 Authorized Users.

issues.quote: Prairie Hollow must pay the annual license fee no later than January 31 of each year.
issues.why: "must" used for a duty of a party that is the subject.

issues.anchor: In the event that Prairie Hollow shall
issues.quote: In the event that Prairie Hollow shall designate more than 40 Authorized Users, Prairie Hollow shall pay Northgate $600 per year for each additional Authorized User.
issues.why: "shall" in a condition (with the wordy "In the event that").
issues.fix: If Prairie Hollow designates more than 40 Authorized Users, ...

issues.quote: If Northgate notices an error in the Software on its own, Northgate shall correct the error in its next scheduled release.
issues.why: "notice" is a term of art (giving notice).

issues.quote: Northgate may suspend support if Prairie Hollow's use of the Software places a substantial load on Northgate's servers.
issues.why: "substantial" is undefined where a measure was possible.

issues.quote: Northgate may conduct 1 audit of Prairie Hollow's use of the Software each year, between January 1 and March 31, if Northgate gives Prairie Hollow notice of the audit at least 10 days before the audit begins.
issues.why: "between" leaves unclear whether January 1 and March 31 are included.
issues.fix: during the period from and including January 1 through March 31

issues.quote: On termination, Prairie Hollow shall cease and desist from using the Software and shall delete all copies of the Software from its computers.
This agreement is binding on the parties and their successors and assigns.

traps.anchor: Northgate is not required to support
traps.quote: Northgate is not required to support any version of the Software other than the current release and the immediately preceding release.
traps.why_correct: House exception to active voice: "is not required to" (MSCD 3.292).

traps.quote: Prairie Hollow shall give Northgate's auditors access to the computers on which Prairie Hollow has installed the Software.
EXCEPT AS THIS AGREEMENT STATES, NORTHGATE DISCLAIMS ALL IMPLIED WARRANTIES, INCLUDING THE IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY AND THE IMPLIED WARRANTY OF FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
traps.why_correct: UCC disclaimer: UCC Section 2-316(2) requires an exclusion of the implied warranty of merchantability to mention merchantability and, in a writing, to be conspicuous. Keep the capitals. Settled policy: statutory wording stays; a note that flags it while keeping it unchanged is acceptable, but rewriting or lowercasing it is an error.

traps.quote: Northgate hereby grants Prairie Hollow a nonexclusive, nontransferable license to install and use Northgate's GrainLedger software, in object-code form (the "Software"), for Prairie Hollow's internal operations at its grain elevators in Kansas.
traps.why_correct: Language of performance uses "hereby" with the simple present (MSCD 3.48-3.50); "hereby" is not on the archaic list.

notes: Unknown drafter.  The paragraph "1. The annual license fee shall be $24,000, ..." under "B. Fees" is wrapped in a block-level content control (<w:sdt><w:sdtPr/><w:sdtContent>...</w:sdtContent></w:sdt>); a reader that skips w:sdt will miss the category-shall issue.  "Northgate hereby grants" is correct language of performance.  Formatting is compliant (Aptos 12, left-aligned).
